edges.rationale: Defining what an application should and should not do establishes the behavioral boundaries and expected outputs that generation quality criteria (fluency, coherence, factual consistency, faithfulness, safety) are designed to measure.
Defining the scope of an application determines which domain-specific capabilities (math, science, reasoning, code generation, tool use) are relevant and should be assessed via benchmarks.

To evaluate quality criteria such as fluency, coherence, and factual consistency, one must first select appropriate scoring methods (classifiers, semantic similarity, AI judges) and define unambiguous rubrics with examples.
Applying domain-specific benchmarks requires selecting evaluation methods and establishing scoring rubrics to interpret benchmark results consistently.
Assessing operational metrics such as cost and latency requires defined measurement methods and scoring guidelines to ensure consistent evaluation alongside quality criteria.
